newsitem.title: USA: Hyatt, Israel Aircraft form business aircraft firm.
newsitem.headline: Hyatt, Israel Aircraft form business aircraft firm.

text.p: Hyatt Corp, a privately-help company owned by the Pritzker family, and Israel Aircraft Industries Ltd (IAI) said they formed Galaxy Aerospace Corp, a new corporate jet manufacturer.

Galaxy Aerospace will produce and market mid-sized business aircraft, including the $10 milion transcontinental business jet currently produced by IAI and the new $14.5 million Galaxy intercontinental jet now under development.
Galaxy representatives declined to comment on Hyatt's investment in the company, but said it will cost $80 million to finish the certification of the new Galaxy business jet.

IAI said it will continue to manufacture the Astra SPX and Galaxy airframes at its Tel Aviv facility. The aircraft will be flown to a U.S. "completion center", where they will be fitted with production engines and interior components.
The completion center will be operational within 12 months. The Galaxy jet is scheduled to begin fligth testing in mid-1997, with certificantion expected in late 1998.
Galaxy expects to produce about 40 jets a year when it hits full production levels in 1999.
Galaxy Aerospace will be led by Brian Barents, who previously served as president and chief executive of Bombardier Inc's Learjet Inc from 1989 to 1996.
